sections.h2: Who does what on a Pasco tax bill
sections.html:
Three elected offices split the work. The appraiser sets values, the collector sends bills and takes payment, and the clerk staffs the appeals board and records your deed.

The appraiser's roll counts 335,946 real property parcels, among them 206,994 single family homes and 11,888 condominium units. Appraiser offices are in Dade City (352-521-4433), Land O' Lakes (813-929-2780) and New Port Richey (727-847-8151).

The Tax Collector has offices in New Port Richey, Gulf Harbors, Land O'Lakes, Wesley Chapel and Dade City. Its tax department answers at 352-521-4338, prompt 3.

  • Pasco County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, taxing districts list, records search.
  • Pasco County Tax Collector: bills, online payment, installment plan, partial payment, delinquent taxes.
  • Pasco County Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and the Official Records.

sections.h2: Due dates and the installment plan
sections.html:
Pasco follows the usual Florida rhythm: a bill in November, discounts through February and delinquency on April 1. The details below come from the collector.

Owners whose estimated tax tops one hundred dollars can use an installment plan. For tax year 2027, forms open November 1, 2026 and the filing cutoff is April 30, 2027; no applications are taken from May 1 through October 31. The first payment has to arrive by July 31 or you drop out of the plan. Each parcel needs its own application, and renewal after that is automatic.

The collector's menu also lists a partial payment application. Before delinquency, state law leaves partial payments to the collector's discretion, so call before you send less than the whole bill.

Installment schedule
PaymentMonth dueDiscount
FirstJune6 percent
SecondSeptember4.5 percent
ThirdDecember3 percent
FourthMarchNone

File once with the Property Appraiser by March 1 and the taxable value of your primary home goes down. The Tax Collector does not handle homestead filings. The appraiser accepts applications all year but applies the March 1 cutoff.

The appraiser's exemptions menu is sorted into six groups: Homestead, Disability, Military and First Responders, Agriculture, Parent and Grandparent, and Senior Aged 65 and older. Under state rules the base homestead benefit is up to $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to school taxes, and the second $25,000 reaches only value above $50,000 for non-school taxes. An added senior exemption exists for some owners if Pasco has approved it and income is under a limit, so ask the appraiser.

A sale or deed ends the capped assessment. A change of ownership returns the parcel to market value at the next valuation date, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. The state's 2026 Save Our Homes cap is printed at 2.7 percent.

  • File by March 1 of the year you want the benefit, with the home already your permanent residence on January 1.
  • Renting the house or moving out ends eligibility.
  • A servicemember may rent out the homestead without losing it under state law.

sections.h2: Other pages worth a look before listing
sections.html:
The collector's menu has a change of mailing address form, an electronic bill and receipt signup, instructions for printing a paid receipt and a page about tax deed sales. On the appraiser's side there is a catastrophic event page, a taxing authorities and districts list and a reporting page for possible homestead fraud.

A storm-damaged or inherited house is a common reason to sell, and those pages explain what relief exists and which districts levy on the parcel.

  • Update your mailing address with the right office before you move so notices reach you.
  • Print the paid receipt for your closing file once the tax is cleared.
  • Use the taxing districts list to see which local districts tax your parcel.

sections.h2: What happens when a Pasco bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
April 1 starts the clock with a late penalty, a lien is sold afterward, and after two years the property can go to public auction.

The penalty is 3 percent of the tax, followed by advertising charges. By the first of June a tax certificate is issued against the parcel for the tax, penalties and costs. Interest on it runs between 5 percent and 18 percent. If the tax is still unpaid after two years, the property may be sold at public auction.

On delinquent bills the collector wants a money order, cashier's check or wire, and takes cash only at its offices. A personal or business check comes back, and the delay can add interest. Escrow checks from an attorney, title company or mortgage broker are accepted.

A certificate buyer is barred by state law from contacting you to demand payment for two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. A stranger calling about your lien that early is a red flag.

sections.h2: How tax is settled at a Pasco sale
sections.html:
You seldom walk a check to the collector yourself, since the closing agent deducts what the parcel owes.

Afterward, the appraiser reports ownership changes through the year. Unpaid tax produces a duplicate notice to the new owner, and delinquent tax a reminder. The owner shown on the collector's website is the owner on the certified tax roll, which is usually finished in early October.

Outside Miami-Dade the state deed tax is 70 cents per $100 of price, and each party to the deed is liable whoever agrees to pay. The clerk quotes the recording charge in its FAQ.

The buyer feels the change, too. A sale resets assessed value, so the new owner's bill can come in well above your capped one. A buyer who will live in the house files for homestead by the next March 1.

Talk to the Property Appraiser first. If you still disagree, petition the Value Adjustment Board, which the Pasco Clerk and Comptroller staffs. A board petition carries a non-refundable $50.00 filing fee under the clerk's FAQ.

Two petitions are different: a portability petition on the DR-486PORT form costs $15.00, and a petition over a denied homestead application, deployed military exemption or tax deferral has no fee. State rules allow 25 days from the proposed-tax notice for a value petition and 30 days from a mailed denial letter for an exemption denial. The notice arrives in August, and the dates on it control.

Business equipment and rental furnishings fall under a tangible personal property return, covered on the appraiser's site. If you rent the house before selling, ask the appraiser whether one applies.

sections.h2: Before you put the house on the market
sections.html:
Look up the parcel, write down what is owed and request a payoff if anything is open. Collect your homestead paperwork and the August notice. If a tax lien or certificate is involved, ask the collector for the redemption figure on a specific closing date, because interest keeps running.

Choosing a cash sale does not remove any of these steps, but it can shorten the calendar since there is no loan approval. Either way, plan for the payoff to come out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Which Pasco County office takes my tax payment?
faqs.a: The Pasco County Tax Collector, through five working offices and an online portal. Tax questions go to 352-521-4338, prompt 3. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but takes no payments.

faqs.q: What does late Pasco County tax cost?
faqs.a: A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. A tax certificate is issued on or before June 1, carrying interest between 5 percent and 18 percent.

faqs.q: Does Pasco County offer a payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, when the estimated tax tops one hundred dollars. The 2027 plan needs an application by April 30, 2027. Payments fall in June, September, December and March, and the first must arrive by July 31.

faqs.q: Does a Pasco homestead pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No, it stays with the owner. The buyer files by March 1, and the sale moves the assessed value up to market level at the next valuation date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pasco County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent tax, with any certificate redemption costs, is settled from your proceeds before the deed passes. The payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's tax department.
